answer: An operator leases one numbered perch on a charted tidal-bore reach. Only that holder may wander the towpath from the head stake to the perch, punching a one-shot itinerary at flood-high posts, carrying a serialled drum skin. When the official bore crest passes an unannounced gauge they strike the skin; a bank logger records the echo off the flood wall and matches skin grain, punch order, and crest curve. A shared perch, reused skin, or early strike is forfeited as one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive perches, N unique skins, and N live bore watches no single walker can cover on the same tide.
